name: RMS Aurelia
blurbs: Five days at sea, a famous family aboard, and one passenger who will not reach port.
Champagne on the upper deck, fog on the water, and a scream that nobody admits to hearing.
The orchestra kept playing. The stewards kept pouring. Somebody kept a secret all the way across the ocean.
A maiden voyage, a fortune in the purser's safe and a guest list that did not add up.
Halfway across the ocean, the band strikes up a waltz and one dancer never returns to the floor.
First class, second chances and a passenger list with one name too many.
The whistle sounds at dawn. By then, the killer hopes to be ashore.
An heiress, a card sharp and a stowaway: someone aboard is not who they claim to be.
The ship's orchestra knows every waltz. The stewards know every secret. Neither is talking.
Somewhere past the halfway mark, a cabin door was found open and a bed not slept in.
The captain's dinner, the last of the champagne, and one empty seat that nobody can explain.
Land is three days off, the radio has gone quiet, and the purser has started counting heads.
motives: the passenger list had one name too many
an old wager from a previous crossing was finally called in
the jewels in the purser's safe were paste, and someone knew why
a shipboard romance had ended badly, twenty crossings ago
the cargo was insured for far more than it was worth
a forged ticket had bought a new name and a new life
the ship's doctor had signed a certificate that should never have been signed
a stolen painting was crossing the ocean in someone else's luggage
an old shipwreck had left one survivor too many
the fortune waiting in New York could only go to one of them
the captain's log for an earlier voyage had been torn out and kept
a card game had ended with a debt nobody could pay
a stowaway had recognised a face from another life
the marriage announced at the captain's table was already one marriage too many
the shipping line would not survive the truth about the last crossing

The {area} held two passengers that night, and only {murderer} walked back to the cabins. The reason was simple: {motive}.
The ocean keeps its secrets, but the {area} did not. {murderer} and {victim} were alone there, because {motive}.
At dawn the stewards found the {area} empty and one passenger missing. {murderer} was already at breakfast, which took some nerve: {motive}.
{murderer} had booked this crossing for one reason and one meeting in the {area}: {motive}.
Everyone else was out to watch the sunset. {murderer} chose the {area} and the company of {victim}, because {motive}.
{victim} never reached port. {murderer} went ashore with a smile and one less worry: {motive}.
